name: Adjectives and Adverbs
description: Adjective order, comparison of adjectives and adverbs, adverb formation and position, and comparative structures.

questions.title: She speaks English very ___.
This exercise is ___ than the previous one.
It was the ___ film I have ever seen.
Which sentence has the adjectives in the natural order?
He drives more ___ than his brother.
The exam was not ___ difficult as we had feared.
Which adverb is irregular in form?
Your handwriting is ___ than mine.
The film was really ___. I could not stop yawning.
I was ___ by the ending of the novel.
He arrived ___ for the interview, which made a bad impression.
This is ___ expensive restaurant in the city.
Which sentence places the frequency adverb correctly?
The weather today is ___ better than yesterday.
Match each adjective with its comparative form.
Match each adjective with the adverb formed from it.
Match each adjective category with its place in a noun phrase.
Match each -ed or -ing adjective with the meaning it carries.
The more you practise, ___ you become.
Her presentation was by far ___ of the day.
He is nowhere near ___ as his reputation suggests.
Which sentence uses 'hardly' correctly?
options: I could hardly hear the speaker at the back.
I could hardly work all night on the report.
She hardly worked and finished everything.
He pushed hardly on the door and it opened.

questions.title: The new flat is twice ___ the old one.
Which sentence about adjectives and adverbs contains a mistake?
The traffic was ___ heavy that we missed the flight.
He ran ___ fast to catch the bus, but he still missed it.
The room was not warm ___ for the baby.
Which sentence shows a difference in meaning between 'late' and 'lately'?
options: I have not seen him lately, and he arrived late again.
I have not seen him late, and he arrived lately again.
She stayed lately at the office.

questions.title: Of the three proposals, this one is ___ realistic.
His explanation was clear, but ___ convincing.
The results were ___ disappointing to everyone involved.
Match each comparative structure with an example of it.
Match each pair of words with the difference in meaning.
pairs: with effort, and almost not at all

questions.title: Match each sentence with the meaning the adverb position creates.
pairs: Only Anna spoke to the manager.
Anna only spoke to the manager.
she did nothing more than speak

questions.title: Match each faulty comparison with the correction it needs.
So convincing ___ that nobody raised an objection.
The scheme proved considerably ___ effective than its designers had claimed.
Which sentence uses an adjective in the predicative position only?
Which sentence shows the correct order of adverbials?
options: She worked quietly in the library all afternoon.
She worked all afternoon quietly in the library manner.
She worked in the library quietly all afternoon manner.
She quietly all afternoon in the library worked.

questions.title: The report was ___ more detailed than the summary suggested.
Which sentence uses a comparative correlative in a formal register?
options: The greater the investment, the faster the recovery.
The more greater investment, the faster recovery.
Greater the investment, faster the recovery is.
The investment greater, the recovery faster.
